content.value_statement: Weak tests hide broken features and create false confidence. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to audit gaps, write meaningful tests, and maintain critical-path coverage.
actual_capabilities: Audits existing test files by line count, assertions, and coverage value.
Classifies tests as stubs, incomplete coverage, or meaningful coverage.
Prioritizes authentication, API authorization, database operations, and other critical paths.
Guides unit, integration, component, and edge-case tests with real assertions.
Defines coverage targets for API routes, services, components, and overall test health.
Provides maintenance checks for obsolete tests, slow tests, coverage drops, and duplicated test code.
limitations: It provides guidance only; it does not ship a runnable test framework or scripts.
It depends on the host project having suitable test tools and fixtures.
It cannot prove coverage quality without running the project test suite.
Coverage targets are general defaults and may need adjustment for each repository.

use_cases.title: Audit Product Coverage
use_cases.description: Find empty tests, weak assertions, missing critical paths, and the highest value coverage work.

use_cases.title: Design Release Test Plans
use_cases.description: Prioritize authentication, authorization, database, API, and user workflow tests before a release.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Feature Tests
use_cases.description: Write meaningful unit, integration, and component tests while reducing unnecessary mocks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository test suite. Identify empty or weak tests, real coverage, critical gaps, and the highest priority work.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Critical Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test plan for the core product flows. Rank authentication, API authorization, database operations, user workflows, and error handling by risk.

prompt_templates.title: Write Meaningful Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: For this feature, write tests with clear assertions for happy paths, failures, boundaries, and persistence checks. Avoid unnecessary mocks.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Test Maintainability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this test suite for slow tests, flaky tests, duplicated fixtures, weak assertions, and code that should be refactored for testability.

output_examples.input: Audit a repository with many small test files.
output: Classifies several files as stubs because they contain few real assertions.
Lists missing tests for authentication, API authorization, and database writes.
Provides an estimated work plan ordered by user and business risk.

output_examples.input: Create tests for a contact creation API.
output: Defines success, validation, authorization, and persistence cases.
Requires checks that the saved record can be read after creation.
Calls out missing fixtures or setup needed before implementation.

output_examples.input: Review ongoing test health before release.
output: Flags slow or flaky suites that should block release decisions.
Identifies obsolete tests and repeated helper code.
Summarizes coverage movement and remaining critical gaps.

best_practices: Start with revenue, authentication, authorization, and data integrity paths before lower-risk behavior.
Prefer assertions that would fail when the feature breaks.
Run tests after changes and investigate failures before expanding coverage.
anti_patterns: Counting empty test files as coverage.
Mocking the behavior being tested when an integration check is practical.
Writing broad tests with vague names and no meaningful assertions.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides test audit, writing, and maintenance. The agent should use project-approved commands when execution is requested.

faq.question: What test types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, component, API, database, authorization, edge-case, and maintenance testing.

faq.question: Can it replace a QA strategy?
faq.answer: No. It helps build practical coverage, but teams still need release criteria and risk ownership.

faq.question: How does it rank test work?
faq.answer: It prioritizes critical paths, security-sensitive flows, business impact, and tests that catch real failures.

faq.question: Does it require a specific framework?
faq.answer: No. It adapts to the repository existing testing tools and conventions.

faq.question: How should teams use coverage targets?
faq.answer: Use targets as guidance, then adjust them for risk, feature maturity, and the cost of reliable tests.
